subject: Architectural alignment & SLO confirmation for ZenReach pilot
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@zenreach.io>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: priya.shah@zenreach.io
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: latency goals, throughput targets, and model fit

Thanks for the demo and deep dive today — quick recap from our side to make sure we captured the right priorities and constraints. Appreciate Ben and Soojin joining.

Key pain points we emphasized:
- Client-facing search experiences are timing out at peak; 95th-percentile p99 search latency can spike above 600ms currently and that’s unacceptable for retention metrics.
- Cost vs. quality tradeoff — we need to support a mix of short-chat-style completions (<=512 tokens) and dense embedding workloads for ranking without runaway spend.
- Data security: logs must be retained for audit but sanitized; we need clear isolation for PII-sensitive pipelines.

Goals for pilot (what we’d like Redwood to prove in a 6-week pilot):
- 95th percentile request latency for single-turn generation under 200ms (target) and stable p99 < 350ms for common prompts
- Embedding throughput of ~120 QPS sustained with amortized cost below our current vendor by 30%
- A deployment topology that fits inside our VPC with clear TLS and KMS integration

Workload profile we shared:
- Generation: 40 QPS typical, bursts to 120 QPS; median prompt length ~60 tokens, 95th up to 800 tokens; target seq length for planning 1024 tokens max
- Embeddings: 120 QPS steady state, small vectors (512–768 dim), batched requests okay with 50–100ms additional batching window
- Authentication: OAuth2 service-to-service and token-scoped API keys for different teams

Questions we have (to confirm in the follow-up):
1) Can you outline a recommended topology (Dedicated vs Private) that meets the latency targets?
2) What model variants you’d propose for a pilot (13B vs 70B; quantization levels)?
3) Estimated GPU sizing and rolling capacity plan for the projected RPS
4) Expected integration work (network peering/VPC setup, certs, KMS, audit logs) — estimate of days required

We’d like to get a short technical follow-up with your solutions engineer to lock the architecture and then confirm commercial terms.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, ZenReach

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@zenreach.io>, priya.shah@zenreach.io
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency goals, throughput targets, and model fit

Sam — great to meet you and thanks for a clear recap. Below I’ll confirm our proposed approach and next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve also attached an initial SLO worksheet and a simple network diagram (PDF/PNG stubs attached).

Short answer to your numbered questions:
1) Topology recommendation (pilot): Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west-2 behind a customer VPC peering. This gives single-tenant GPU capacity and predictable p99 latency while allowing KMS/HSM for key material. For the pilot we recommend a small reserved pool with autoscale thresholds and burst capacity to handle your traffic bursts.

Architecture sketch (high level):
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) in us-west-2 with VPC peering to your network; control plane remains in Redwood-hosted region (no customer data plane leaves your VPC).
- Load-router with latency-aware routing + fallback to smaller model family for tail events.
- KV cache (prefix-level) on the serving layer to avoid repeated KV rebuilds for common prompts.
- Batching window set conservatively to 15–25ms for generation to preserve latency; embeddings batched up to 128 items when beneficial.

Model recommendations for pilot:
- Primary: 13B/14B sequence model quantized to int8 (saves memory and maintains most generation quality for your prompt lengths).
- Fallback: 7B int8 for ultra-low-latency fallbacks and cold-start handling.
- Embeddings: a dedicated 3B embeddings model with batched inference and vector post-processing; we’ll ensure dimensionality matches your downstream ranker (we recommend 768 dims).

Sizing & latency estimates (initial):
- Generation: estimate 4x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (in a small pool) to meet 40 QPS with target p95 < 120ms and p99 < 300ms for median prompt (60 tokens); to sustain bursts to 120 QPS we recommend burst capacity or autoscaled extra 4 GPUs.
- Embeddings: with batching (batch=64) and int8 inference, 2x high-memory GPUs should comfortably support 120 QPS with average latency ~60–90ms.
- KV cache memory: budget ~24–32GB of RAM across the pool for common prefixes (~100K keys) depending on your shard strategy.

Quality vs cost knobs we’ll use:
- Quantization profile per-model (float16 for high-quality routes; int8 for cost-sensitive fallbacks)
- Adaptive batching per-endpoint: embeddings aggressively batched, generation prioritized for low-latency requests
- Route-level SLOs: pin critical routes to dedicated resources to avoid noisy neighbor issues

Integration effort & timeline (ballpark):
- VPC peering + KMS setup: 3–5 business days with your infra team (one coordinated maintenance window).
- Initial model onboarding and tuning (pilot): 1–2 weeks (we’ll run a small prompt set and QA).
- Pilot validation and reporting to agree SLOs: 2–3 weeks of data collection.

Next steps I suggest:
- Technical touchpoint: 60-min deep-dive this week to finalize exact GPU types and batch sizing (I’ll bring Marissa).
- Commercial: Ben will share a pilot pricing estimate and a simple SLA addendum for the pilot period.

I’ve attached: zenreach_slo_requirements.pdf (your doc annotated), zenreach_network_diagram.png (sketch), redwood-dedicated-estimate.xlsx (ballpark).

If that looks right, can we lock a follow-up slot? I’m available Wed/Thu PST afternoons.

— Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — that reads well and aligns with our expectations. A couple quick clarifications before we lock calendar: 

- Latency: the p95 < 200ms target is priority; p99 < 350ms is acceptable for the pilot but we’ll want to push p99 lower over time.
- Security: we require KMS integration and audit logs stored for 90 days; can you confirm retention controls are configurable per-customer?
- Pilot start: we can kick off as early as June 26th if the SOW and network prep are ready.

Can we book the 60-min technical alignment on Wednesday (June 14th) at 2pm PST? If Soojin and Marissa can make that, we’ll lock the pilot start date and Ben can send the SOW for signature.
